nonempty-choice: Proof 1.1 fixes the admissible normalising series and transports homogeneous summands; 2.1 compares two given series. The Remarks explicitly identify these constructions as finite and choice-free.
iff-forward: Transporting homogeneous KLR summands along the fixed block isomorphism constructs a grading with prescribed generator degrees; this grading assertion is not a criterion characterizing when a block exists.
iff-reverse: Uniqueness for fixed generator images and graded isomorphism between two transported gradings do not assert that any grading recovers a normalising series. No reverse characterization is claimed.
endpoints: The grading consists of integer-indexed homogeneous summands and fixed finite quantum characteristic, with no limiting specialization of the Hecke parameter or convergence assertion.
degenerate: Proof 2.3 explicitly includes the characteristic-two degeneration: the surviving rank-two sector is the dual-number algebra with its dot in degree two. Trivial block gradings are separately allowed by 2.2.
zero: Proof 1.1 assigns residue idempotents degree zero and transports the direct sum without dividing by a degree; 2.2 explicitly permits a block supported entirely in degree zero.
empty: The consumed isomorphism in F1 concerns content with nonzero block idempotent, so an absent Hecke block is excluded. Zero homogeneous summands in the transported decomposition require no additional construction.

iff-forward: Local finiteness specifies which formal singular chains constitute the chain module; the subsequent boundary and proper-pushforward constructions do not assert an equivalence between two homology theories.
iff-reverse: Proper maps are given a chain pushforward by composition with simplices. The Definition does not conversely characterize properness by the existence of a pushforward or equate arbitrary locally finite and finite chains.

empty: In root degree zero the color scalar is an empty product equal to the unit; the Definition also fixes counit normalization on the two units, so the empty root word introduces no denominator.
zero: The Definition sets the pairing to zero when the two degrees are not opposite, and bilinearity gives zero on a zero vector. Its degree-zero counit value is explicitly the unit.
one: The Definition explicitly gives the simple-generator pairing as the Kronecker value divided by the quantum difference and separately gives the pairing of the two units; the divided-power formula specializes to these generator values.
degenerate: The normalization divides by quantum differences in the rational quantum parameter field. No specialization to a root of unity, where those denominators could vanish, is asserted in this Definition.
endpoints: This algebraic pairing rescales each root-degree component of the Kashiwara form and defines simple-root toral pairings; there is no analytic parameter limit or interval endpoint assertion.
iff-reverse: Transporting the half form with the stated root-degree scalar defines a particular pairing. It does not claim that any bilinear pairing satisfying some subset of the displayed values must arise by that transport.
nonempty-choice: The pairing is given directly by the transported Kashiwara form and a finite color-degree product. The reference to dual bases concerns the completed tensor supplier, and this Definition itself selects no basis or arbitrary family.
iff-forward: The assignment of the root-degree-rescaled half form and its generator normalization is a definition followed by values; it is not a biconditional criterion for a vector to belong to either quantum half.

A projective endofunctor is defined by being isomorphic to a direct summand of a finite-dimensional tensor functor followed by block projection; exactness and preservation of projectives are stated as resulting properties, not an equivalent criterion.
iff-reverse: The Definition does not assert that every exact endofunctor preserving projective objects is a summand of a tensor-and-projection functor. The direct-summand construction fixes the class rather than giving such a converse.
endpoints: The fixed regular integral block, finite-dimensional tensor module and idempotent summand data are categorical inputs; no wall limit, interval endpoint or parameter-specialization assertion belongs to this Definition.

empty: The rank-one formulas in proof 1.1 use factorials and norm products; at exponent zero those products are empty and equal the unit, giving the unit lower vector and unit norm.
zero: At rank-one exponent zero, proof 1.1 gives the zeroth divided power as the unit and both normalization factors as unit empty products. The Example does not specialize the formal quantum parameter to a singular scalar.
degenerate: Proof 2.1 computes the mixed-degree Gram determinant as the nonzero formal polynomial one minus the square of the quantum parameter, and 3.1 inverts it over the field. Singular scalar specialization of that matrix is outside the Example.
endpoints: The modulo-quantum-parameter residue comparison and the field inverse Gram matrix are algebraic normalizations, with no limit as the parameter approaches a scalar and no endpoint continuity claim.

iff-reverse: The Example states the highest-vertex criterion as an equivalence. Verification 2.1 checks that each of the two surviving tensor vertices satisfies both epsilon inequalities, while 2.2 shows the rejected third candidate is raised nontrivially.

iff-forward: The Example calculates a PBW rank, explicit unequal-color crossing actions and projective class identities in two prescribed Cartan cases; none is posed as a biconditional recognizing a KLR datum.
iff-reverse: The displayed commuting projective classes and simply-laced Serre relation are consequences of the selected polynomial parameters. No converse inferring the Cartan entry or factorization from these class identities is asserted.
nonempty-choice: Verification 2.1 uses the explicitly displayed linear factor and constant factor, and 1.1 lists the four PBW families. There is no arbitrary selection from a family of factorizations.
degenerate: Verification 1.2 treats the disconnected Cartan case: the crossing squares to the unit and right multiplication by it gives inverse projective-module maps. The connected linear-parameter case is checked separately in 2.1.
one: For the constant unit polynomial in verification 1.2, the crossing is an involution and both right-multiplication composites are the identity on their idempotent corners. Thus the unit parameter case is explicitly treated.
empty: The fixed weight contains two distinct simple roots and has exactly the two displayed words; its polynomial representation has two nonempty idempotent summands, and no empty-word weight is part of this Example.

one: The allowed single-component case has a single height-matrix column. Proof 1.3 fixes every entry through its row sums, so each fixed-margin class is a singleton, and the minimum and connectivity arguments have no distinct-column switch to perform.
nonempty-choice: Proof 3.1 starts from a given matrix in a nonempty fixed-hub class and descends through finite zero-switch paths until nonnegative size cannot decrease. Proof 4.1 chooses entries in finite binary matrices; no infinite family is selected.
iff-forward: The Statement explicitly equates equal content with equal hubs and equal size. Equal residue-count vectors have the same total node count and, by the boundary identity of proof 1.2, the same removable-minus-addable hub.
iff-reverse: Proof 2.1 takes the difference of the residue-count vectors for equal hubs; the cyclic Laplacian makes that difference constant. Equal total size forces the constant to vanish, giving equal content as asserted.
endpoints: Minimum size is the extremal boundary relevant to descent. Proof 3.1 identifies balanced shifted rows with global minima and proves descent terminates in nonnegative integer core size; proof 4.1 handles connectivity at that minimum.
degenerate: At quantum characteristic two the neighboring residues coincide. Proof 1.2 expressly retains both boundary-count contributions and counts that neighbor twice, which is the double-edge convention required by the Statement.
empty: Proof 1.2 begins with the empty multipartition: all residue counts vanish and each component contributes its first addable node, giving the initial hub as the negative charge multiplicity vector.
zero: The induction base of proof 1.2 has zero size and zero residue counts. Zero-energy switches are also explicitly identified in 1.4 and used in 3.1 and 4.1 without changing the associated core size.

iff-reverse: The conclusion bounds the cardinality of the real zero set from a nonzero leading coefficient. It does not conversely infer a coefficient-list degree or a nonzero leading coefficient from having finitely many real roots.

iff-forward: The four Statement clauses assert an action-algebra isomorphism, Hom freeness, base-change compatibility and special-fiber detection; none asserts a biconditional classification of deformed-family objects.
iff-reverse: The special-fiber clause is stated as the sufficient direction from an invertible special fiber to an invertible map, proved by local weight-space determinants in 4.1. There is no separately claimed reverse criterion to discharge.

nonempty-choice: At positive quotient weight, proof 1.1 obtains a removable quotient box from a finite partition and 2.2 instantiates one corresponding border strip. The induction decreases finite weight; the Statement expressly disclaims a choice principle.

iff-forward: The Statement constructs exact induction and restriction functors, their adjoints and a Mackey filtration from specified KLR block bimodules; it does not present an equivalence testing when two arbitrary functors have those properties.
iff-reverse: The second-adjunction formula reverses the blocks and carries the pairing shift. It is a functor isomorphism, not a converse saying an unshifted same-order biadjunction characterizes the KLR datum.
endpoints: The filtration is indexed by finitely many four-block weight matrices, and its degree shift is the root pairing. No continuous endpoint or asymptotic parameter limit enters these finite shuffle statements.
nonempty-choice: Proof 1.1 selects reduced words for a finite permutation group and uses explicitly indexed shuffle summands; 3.1 performs finite triangular elimination with unit diagonal. These finite choices require no arbitrary-index choice principle.
degenerate: If a block weight is zero, the consumed KLR Definition gives the field algebra in that weight. The shuffle decomposition in 1.1 then has only the identity shuffle, and the block-pairing shift of 2.2 is zero.
one: When the shuffle rank is one, proof 1.1 consists of the single identity representative, so its sum over source idempotents is one ungraded block-algebra copy. The tensor-Hom maps of 1.2 still apply without a crossing.
zero: Weights are allowed in the positive root monoid including zero. With a zero block, the field convention and the unique empty-block shuffle in 1.1 give the unit induction/restriction case; the longest-shuffle pairing in 2.2 has zero degree.

iff-forward: The Statement identifies lower global vectors with normalized self-dual projective shift orbits under the categorification map. This is a basis bijection in the specified geometric parameter regime, not a biconditional hypothesis on arbitrary parameters.
iff-reverse: Proof 3.1 exhausts indecomposable projective orbits using simple perverse summands, and 4.1 exhausts the signed global vectors before 5.1 fixes signs. That surjectivity belongs to the stated bijection, not a reverse parameter-characterization theorem.

degenerate: Proof 1.1 explicitly keeps the factorization nonzero when an arrow multiplicity vanishes: its corresponding factor is the constant unit. Thus disconnected quiver directions are included, while the Statement excludes unrelated parameter changes.
one: Quivers with a single vertex are allowed, but the Statement imposes no separate rank-one conclusion: the geometric comparison, Yoneda equivalence and positive first-string argument use the same symmetric quiver assumptions in that scope.
zero: The consumed KLR Definition includes the zero-weight algebra as the field. At that weight proof 1.1 has the empty-word polynomial summand, and the regular projective in 2.2 has unit scalar endomorphisms; the norm and sign normalization retain the global unit.

iff-forward: The theorem verifies the Coxeter, cross and polynomial relations for the specified Casimir and place-permutation operators and thereby constructs an action; it is not an equivalence characterizing arbitrary operator families.
iff-reverse: The construction in proof 3.1 turns the verified left Hecke action into a right action using the generator-fixing anti-involution. No converse recovering a matrix-Lie-algebra tensor functor from a Hecke action is claimed.
one: The dimension hypothesis permits the one-dimensional natural module. The matrix-unit identities in 1.1 remain valid with one summation index, and for tensor degree one the operator sum has no earlier natural-factor permutations.
degenerate: For tensor degree zero or one there are no adjacent-place generators, so the Coxeter and cross relations of 1.2 and 2.1 have no admissible indices. The remaining scalar or single polynomial action is obtained by the same construction in 3.1.

zero: The Given explicitly allows tensor degree zero, when the tensor functor is the original module and there are no polynomial or adjacent-place operators. Proof 3.1 supplies the scalar right action; a zero input module is also preserved by every displayed linear operator.
